postconditions.satisfied_by: JUDGEMENT CALL 1 (regression guard shape): replaced test_dirty_lives_in_run_not_content with test_dirty_appears_nowhere_in_the_manifest. Chose a DEPTH-COMPLETE guard over three flat assertions: not in run, not in repo_rev, not in content(), PLUS a new module-level helper _dirty_key_paths() that walks the whole envelope (dicts and lists) and must return [], PLUS 'dirty' not in cm.encode(m). Rationale: three flat assertions only guard the three places the field has historically lived; the recursive sweep + encoded-token check also catch a re-introduction under a nested or renamed parent, which is the regression that would otherwise land silently. The repo_state fake still supplies dirty=True. JUDGEMENT CALL 2 (test_content_is_unaffected_by_dirty_when_commit_is_equal): KEPT the test and TOOK the handoff's suggested strengthening. Dropped the final assertNotEqual on the two run.dirty values (no subject) and replaced it with two assertions that the WHOLE manifest is now insensitive to dirty: run subtrees equal modulo generated_at, and everything outside run equal outright. Rationale: the old test could only claim content-insensitivity because the manifests genuinely differed elsewhere; with the field dropped that weaker claim understates what is now true, and the stronger form is the one that would catch dirty leaking back in under any key. Compared modulo generated_at only -- roots/host/cwd are constant within one process, so nothing else is legitimately free to move. ALSO (not flagged by the handoff): removed the now-dead status_oracle subprocess block from test_default_repo_state_against_the_real_repo_matches_git_oracles and renamed it ..._matches_the_commit_oracle (singular); leaving a plural name over one oracle is exactly the stale description the handoff forbids. Verified by grep that no tracked file outside .agent-work archives references either renamed test id. Same reasoning renamed the two ..._yields_none_none tests to ..._yields_no_commit.
